subject: Commercial packaging for HelixBio VPC pilot — operator license / SRE retainer options
messages:
From: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@helixbio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixbio.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC pilot packaging questions and ask on operator credits

Kim — thanks for yesterday's demo. We like Redwood's performance profile, but before we move to an internal approval I need one thing clarified from a commercial standpoint. We're planning a 6-month single-tenant VPC pilot across two sites (US-East and US-West) with the intention to expand if results look good. Two items from procurement that are blocking our approval: 

1) Platform fee: our CFO is concerned about the fixed platform fee during a pilot. Can you show an amortized option or a partial credit if we commit to a 12-month follow-on within 90 days of pilot completion?

2) Operator licenses / SRE retainer: We run our own infra but will need Redwood on-call for the first 8 weeks of the pilot. Can you propose an operator-license offset (e.g., reduce platform fee in exchange for a limited retainer) or a short-term SRE retainer SKU we can buy for the pilot period?

Attachments: procurement asked for a simple term-sheet and SOW example if possible. Can you share?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Elliot Turner
Head of Platform Engineering
HelixBio

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@helixbio.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC pilot packaging questions and ask on operator credits

Elliot — thanks for the clear summary and the great conversation yesterday. Short answers up front, then a proposal below.

1) Platform fee amortization: We can offer a pilot-to-production credit. If HelixBio signs a 12-month Private deployment agreement within 90 days after pilot sign-off, we will credit 50% of the pilot platform fee against the first 3 months of the annual platform fee (applied as invoice credit). We can show the math in the term-sheet.

2) Operator license / SRE retainer: Two options we commonly use:
  - Option A (retainer SKU): 8-week SRE retainer at a fixed daily rate (prepaid) covering on-call + 4 guaranteed response hours/day. This preserves platform fee but gives predictable ops coverage.
  - Option B (operator-offset): Convert up to 2 operator licenses into a temporary platform-fee discount equal to the monthly operator license cost for the pilot duration (effectively reducing pilot platform fee dollar-for-dollar).

I've attached a draft term-sheet and a sample SOW for the pilot, plus our support tiers spreadsheet so procurement can see breakouts.

Would you prefer Option A or B? If you want, we can combine them (smaller retainer + partial offset).

Next step: I'll loop in Pricing to prepare a formal quote once you confirm the preferred approach and expected pilot daily token volumes (so we size the reserved capacity).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@helixbio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixbio.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC pilot packaging questions and ask on operator credits

Kim — appreciate the quick reply and the term-sheet. Procurement prefers Option B (operator-offset) because it keeps the pilot cashflow lighter and aligns incentives — we only want to pay incremental SRE if there's real work. Two follow-ups:

• Can the offset be applied to platform fee so it reduces our pilot invoice immediately (not an internal rebate)? Procurement needs net invoice reduction, not paper credits.

• For the 12-month follow-on credit you mentioned: could you increase the pilot-credit from 50% to 65% if we commit to a 2-year contract v. 1-year? Our CFO is wary about lock-in but might accept a longer commitment with a better credit.

Also — we're estimating token usage of ~120M tokens/month during pilot peak. Please sanity-check capacity assumptions and any node sizing you'd recommend.

Elliot

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: HelixBio pilot — commercial options and ask

Kim / Marissa — filing notes from Elliot's ask. He prefers operator-offset (Option B) and wants the offset applied as an immediate reduction to the pilot invoice (not deferred credit). He also pushed for a higher pilot-to-production credit (65%) if HelixBio signs a 2-year follow-on. Token estimate: 120M/month.

Questions for Pricing/Commercial team:
1) Can we structure operator-offset as a defined discount on the pilot invoice (i.e., remove N operator licenses cost from invoice) without creating downstream accounting headaches?
2) If we increase the follow-on credit to 65% for a 2-year commit, what approval level do we need? Any revenue-metrics or legal constraints?
3) Node sizing: for 120M tokens/month across two sites (pilot windows), recommended configuration? We should propose a small burst pool + 2 dedicated nodes for steady state — cost/sku to show.

I'll draft a short counter-proposal for Helix to review once we have Pricing permissions.

— Priyom
Head of Commercial Strategy (cc: AE)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBio pilot — commercial options and ask

Thanks for the summary. Quick legal / procurement notes: 

• Operator-offset as invoice reduction: acceptable if we treat operator licenses as a separately priced SKU that we can zero out on the pilot invoice. Accounting prefers a clear line item "Operator licenses (pilot) — $XX" with negative pricing applied. That keeps the ARR math clean.

• Increasing pilot credit to 65% for a 2-year commit: requires Director-level approval in Commercial (I'll take this to Revenue Ops). We should condition the higher credit on a minimum committed monthly token floor (e.g., 100M tokens/mo) and an early-exit recoup clause.

• Node sizing comment for Pricing: recommend we include an elastic burst credit for first 30 days to avoid throttling spikes, then transition to the reserved node footprint. I'll attach a quick pricing worksheet for the quote.

Action items: Marissa will route Director approval for 65% credit contingency. Priyom to draft a short counter-proposal that shows: (a) pilot invoice with operator-offset applied, (b) 2-year follow-on with 65% pilot credit conditional on token floor, (c) recommended node SKUs + burst credit for first 30 days. Kimberly to schedule a 30-minute call with Elliot and procurement for Friday to finalize.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Structuring
Redwood Inference
